annotation.surface: Someone with a holiday cottage who wastes money now and again finally tightens their belt.

entries.clue: Stingy individual back on cheaper booze (4)

annotation.surface: A tightwad sticking to the cheap stuff at the bar.

annotation.definitionFit: Plain membership: booze is any alcoholic drink, and beer is the commonest kind.

entries.clue: Rolls with wedges, maybe? (6)

blocks.note: W is the standard abbreviation for with
a wedge is one kind of shoe heel, so 'maybe' marks an example

annotation.surface: A lunch order: bread rolls with a side of potato wedges.
annotation.walkthrough: The food surface makes 'Rolls' a noun, bread; it is the verb, to turn over and over along the ground.
annotation.definitionFit: To wheel a trolley is to roll it along, so wheels and rolls are synonymous verbs.

entries.clue: Date leaves for tastier dinner, we hear (4)

indicatorNotes.we hear: what we hear is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: thyme is a herb whose leaves flavour food

annotation.surface: A cook's tip about herbs to make the evening meal more flavourful.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Date' sits at the front looking like the fruit in a recipe; it is the definition, a point in time.
annotation.definitionFit: A date is a particular time, as in 'set a date' or 'set a time'.

entries.clue: Many characters of a certain age put on these (7)

annotation.definition: Many characters of a certain age put on these

blocks.clueFragment: Many characters of a certain age
blocks.note: read as lots of elderly people, and meant as the written signs of an ancient era, cuneiform pressed into clay
read as the pills older people are prescribed, and meant as the slabs those characters were inscribed on

annotation.surface: Elderly people and the pills they are put on.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests old people put on medication; in fact ancient writing was pressed onto clay, so the characters are letters from a certain age.
annotation.definitionFit: Ancient scribes put their written characters on clay or stone slabs, so these are what the characters went on.

entries.clue: Ancient people some spot playing around – is Methuselah one? (13)

indicatorNotes.around: the jumbled letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: SOME SPOT jumbled
the setter, Methuselah, asking about himself: 'Am I an (ancient person)?'

annotation.surface: A search for old folk in a spot where people play, ending with a question about the setter's age.
annotation.walkthrough: Methuselah is this puzzle's setter, named for the long-lived biblical figure, so 'is Methuselah one?' becomes the setter's own question, AM I AN.
annotation.definitionFit: Mesopotamia, between the Tigris and Euphrates, was home to Sumer and Babylon, so its people are the ancient people in question.

entries.clue: Sea creature protects a bit of land (4)

indicatorNotes.protects: to protect something is to hold it safe inside, so the words hold the answer within them

blocks.note: seA CREature

annotation.surface: A marine animal guarding its patch of ground.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Sea creature' a whole noun phrase; the last letter of one word and the start of the next carry the answer across the gap.
annotation.definitionFit: A unit of land area, 4,840 square yards, makes a modest plot: a bit of land by measure.

entries.clue: Hairy swinger opening hotel (5)

blocks.note: a slot is an opening
H is Hotel in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A shaggy man-about-town at a hotel launch party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partygoer; the sloth swings slowly from branches.
annotation.definitionFit: A sloth is a shaggy-coated animal that hangs and swings from trees.

entries.clue: One charged after boosting of two vehicles initially tried taking off (11)

indicatorNotes.boosting: lifting up: in a down entry the letters rise and read backwards

indicatorNotes.after: the charged piece comes after the rest

blocks.note: the first letter of Tried
CART and BUS
an ion is a charged particle

annotation.surface: A car thief is charged after stealing two vehicles and trying to drive off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boosting' is slang for stealing cars, which drives the surface; here it lifts T, CART and BUS up the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: in arithmetic, taking one number off another is subtraction.

entries.clue: Perhaps Benjamin Button arranged loan in obscure language (3,10)

blocks.note: Benjamin Button, in the story and film, is born an old man

annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Benjamin Button as one example of an old baby.
annotation.definitionFit: Old Babylonian is an early form of Akkadian, a dead language known now only to specialists.

entries.clue: Wedding guest trashed basement after dropping an E (4,3)

annotation.surface: A wedding guest who, having had one too many, wrecks the basement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'An E' is exact: BASEMENT has two Es and only one goes.
annotation.definitionFit: The best man is the groom's chief supporter and a guest at the wedding.

entries.clue: A couple of postgraduates penning article on movement's figure study (11)

blocks.note: two MAs, Masters of Arts
the definite article, placed between the two MAs
tics are involuntary movements; movement's reads as movements

annotation.surface: Two graduate students writing a paper about a political movement's leading figure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person; it means numbers. 'Movement's' is read as the plural, tics.
annotation.definitionFit: Figures here are numbers, and the study of numbers is mathematics: a definition in cryptic dress.

entries.clue: Bats agreed to welcome black hawk after name change (7)

B for black, as on pencils

annotation.surface: Bats and a black hawk rename themselves after an agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bats' and 'hawk' pose as two flying creatures; one is an indicator, the other means to sell.
annotation.definitionFit: To rebadge is to sell a product under a new brand name.

entries.clue: Old dad ultimately upset one's left home (5)

pa is dad
the last letter of upseT

annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a sad father whose child has moved away; 'one's' expands to 'one who has'.
annotation.definitionFit: An expat is someone who has left their home country to live abroad.

entries.clue: Turkey gobbles behind short male bullies? (9)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Gobbles' is the noise of a turkey in the surface; here it means eats.
annotation.definitionFit: Maltreats means treats cruelly, which is what a bully does.

annotation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country; it is the verb to say.
annotation.definitionFit: Literature is written works, the kind published on paper.

entries.clue: Club supporters of course part of the furniture (7)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Part of the furniture' is an idiom for someone who has always been around; here it is literal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain membership: sofas are among the items that make up a room's furniture.

entries.clue: On sites for puzzling, most like the Inquisitor (7)

annotation.surface: Websites for solving puzzles, and one puzzle in particular, the Inquisitor.

annotation.definitionFit: An inquisitor asks endless questions, so to be most like one is to be nosiest.

entries.clue: Mark Antony's second only to bloody revolutionary chief (9)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Mark Antony' reads as the Roman general; split it and Mark is punctuation. 'To' is a link here, not a joining signal.

entries.clue: I spy it go snap or squash? (4)

annotation.walkthrough: Each item is a pastime: I spy, it (tag), go (the Japanese board game), snap (a card game) and squash; read as a sentence it looks like an instruction.
